object_types.name: Shipment
object_types.definition: A consignment of products transported through the logistics network, identified by a unique shipment number.

source_references.excerpt: We track shipments -- consignments, some of the older staff say, same thing. Each shipment has a shipment number.

object_types.name: ShipmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Product
object_types.definition: An item that can be included in shipments, identified by a SKU.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.

object_types.name: SKU
object_types.definition: The stock-keeping unit that uniquely identifies a product.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Quantity
object_types.definition: The number of units of a product in a shipment.

source_references.excerpt: A shipment contains products, each in a specific quantity.
For example, shipment S-100 contains product P-77 in quantity 5.

object_types.name: Warehouse
object_types.definition: A physical storage location where shipments may be held, identified by a warehouse code.

source_references.excerpt: Warehouses have a warehouse code.

object_types.name: WarehouseCode
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a warehouse.

ambiguities.description: Identification of Product by SKU: The SKU is stated as the identifier, but whether it is globally unique or only unique within a specific context (e.g., per vendor, per category) is not clarified. The model assumes global uniqueness.

source_references.excerpt: Products are identified by SKU.

ambiguities.description: Shipment identification by ShipmentNumber: While a shipment number is stated, there is no confirmation of uniqueness (e.g., whether a shipment number can be reused after closure, whether it is globally unique, or scoped to a time period). The model assumes permanent global uniqueness.

source_references.excerpt: Each shipment has a shipment number.

ambiguities.description: Cardinality of shipment-to-product containment: The transcript explicitly states 'for a given shipment and product there is exactly one quantity line', confirming uniqueness on the (Shipment, Product) combination. However, it is not explicitly stated whether the Product role itself is mandatory (i.e., whether a shipment can exist without products) or optional. The model does not assume mandatory participation of Product.

ambiguities.description: Warehouse storage bidirectional cardinality: The constraint states a Shipment sits in at most 2 warehouses with a minimum of 1. However, it is not stated whether a Warehouse can store multiple Shipments (assumed yes by domain logic) or whether there are any constraints on how many Shipments a Warehouse can store. The model assumes Warehouses can store multiple Shipments with no upper limit.
